lines.text: Four hundred and thirty-two of them. And the twins out in front. Oakhaven. Day fifteen. The sun was going down when the count came in. Six to one. Let him in. Reyes opened the gate with the dead already moving on Mill Street.
Much obliged, friend. I won't be any trouble.

He took a spot by the east fence, and he didn't move from it all night. Forty of us on the fence. Every floodlight on. Jaylozy, with the fire axe. Seth, with the maul. Jeremy, the bayonet spear. Francis, the boat hook. Jack, on the rifle. Toast, on the machine gun. Asa, with his axe. Tanny and Marco had told us which side they'd come from. Hudson and Johnny's traps, built from the Tilt-A-Whirl, were waiting along the wall. They came out of the dark from the east, right where the scouts said. The floodlights caught them in the open. The shooters opened up. The traps took the first wave. All night, the line held. Near midnight, the twins reached the east fence. They stopped. They looked right at Elias. Then they turned, and walked back into the dark.

Down the line, one of them got an arm through the slats. Javier took a scratch across the forearm. Just a scratch. By morning, the dead were piled up everywhere along the fence. The fence was at eighty-five percent. We didn't lose anyone. The cabin won the vote. When the dust finally settled, Sam, Albin and John set out. They found two full rain barrels out back. Water for one more day. One more day of food and water, and the next horde in six. Where do we go? The gas station, cold storage, or the cattle in the woods?
